changedBeliefs: Exp 229's categorical claim that out-of-lined ISA-specific kernels are viable is now bounded: viable for BULK per-cell payloads (base64 amortises SIMD setup over an entire BLOB per call), NOT for SCALAR per-cell values. An AArch64/NEON i64→decimal kernel (magnitude split into low8/mid8/high groups via two /1e8 divides, each 8-digit group formatted with vector reciprocal splits (d*5243)>>19 and (p*205)>>11, out-of-lined and gated ≥ 1e8, byte-identical to the exp 192 scalar path) converts exactly one integer per call, so the call boundary + vector setup is paid per cell with nothing to amortise it against.

The scalar two-digit-table itoa (exp 192) is confirmed as the floor for per-cell integer JSON encoding under the row-at-a-time architecture. Across 11 focused A/B passes in three methodologies (interleaved both orders, 5-round min-of-N) the 10k×20 ~18-digit BIGINT selectBytes lane never leaned candidate-faster: +1.2/+6.0/+9.8% (baseline-first), +28/+36/+16% (candidate-first, machine at its loudest), +11.3% at min-of-N, and only ~flat (-0.6%, within noise) in the single quiet pair. Identical-code control lanes drifted ±10-120% in the same session, confirming environmental noise rather than a code effect.

Inlining the kernel to remove the call boundary is the wrong fix and was not tried on evidence from exp 229/230: leaking SIMD/vector state into a hot scalar path regresses its code generation, and here it would bloat the per-cell write_json_to_buf loop and hurt the common small-int case that never needs the kernel.
nextSignals: Keep the scalar two-digit-table itoa as the canonical integer JSON formatter. Do not retry a per-cell integer SIMD kernel — the amortisation floor, not the digit algorithm, is what sinks it. `benchmark/experiments/select_bytes_int_heavy.dart` (exp 192) with its BIGINT lane remains the durable gate.

Reopen integer-encode SIMD only if a future architecture batches many integer cells into ONE encode call (a columnar/bulk-step transfer handing the kernel an i64 array), or a production profile shows integer-heavy selectBytes dominating wall enough to justify a non-per-cell-dispatch mechanism.

The i64 differential test (`resqlite_test_i64_to_str` + the `native i64 formatter differential` group in `test/native_encoder_diff_test.dart`) is now the byte-identity gate for the integer formatter — boundary magnitudes, an 8-digit-group sweep, and 300k random full-range i64. Any future integer-encode change must keep it green.
